title: load_testing plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `load_testing` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component LoadTestingConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

LoadTestingConfig.description:
Plugin: load_testing — On-demand proxy load testing triggered by
X-Loadtesting-Key header. Spawns concurrent clients through the
gateway's own proxy listener (HTTP only). Unknown top-level keys are
rejected. File, admin/database, and CP/DP admission share the same
constructor validation; serving-mode publication uses KeepLastKnownGood
so an invalid candidate keeps the prior valid generation active.
Omitted optional fields select defaults; runtime also treats explicit
null on optional fields as omitted. Matching replay bodies have a hard
10 MiB plugin-local ceiling and active local/fan-out replay work shares
a 64 MiB process-wide retained-body budget. Synthetic and fan-out
headers reuse the canonical secondary-request sanitizer shared with
request_mirror (Connection-listed hop-by-hop, Trailer, framing, Ferrum
markers, proxy-owned X-Forwarded-*), preserving Host for routing. That
snapshot is taken from the original client headers, not from the
already-transformed map, so an earlier request_transformer chain is
applied exactly once to the synthetic cohort as well. Synthetic and
fan-out requests are sent over HTTP/1.1 so the preserved Host is the
request authority; over HTTP/2 the two would disagree and ingress
validation would correctly reject every replay. A trigger declaring a
Content-Length above the 10 MiB replay ceiling is not buffered: it is
forwarded under the ordinary request-body limits and no load test
starts. Known limitation: an undeclared-length (chunked, or H2/H3
without Content-Length) trigger body above 10 MiB is refused with 413,
since the ceiling also bounds collection. Fan-out peers acknowledge an admitted trigger with 204
plus X-Loadtesting-Ack echoing the controller's X-Loadtesting-Run-Id;
a request carrying X-Loadtesting-Fanout whose key fails is refused
with 403 before backend dispatch.

key.description: Secret value that the X-Loadtesting-Key header must match to trigger the load test. Must be a randomly generated secret of at least 32 printable ASCII HTTP field-value characters with no leading or trailing space. The gateway never echoes the value in validation errors and strips this reserved header on matching and non-matching paths before later deferred plugins or backend dispatch. Underscore spellings (X_Loadtesting_Key and similar), which CGI-style backends fold onto the same variable, are stripped and redacted too but never authenticate a trigger.

duration_seconds.description: How long the test runs in seconds

ramp.description: When true, clients start gradually over the duration instead of all at once

request_timeout_ms.description: Per-request timeout in milliseconds (1–60000). Each attempt is also capped to the remaining absolute run deadline so workers cannot outlive duration_seconds.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Maximum response bytes the synthetic client consumes per request (1–18446744073709551615). The runtime parses this as an unsigned 64-bit integer, so the finite upper bound is part of the admitted contract; a larger value is rejected. The client stops reading at the cap, bounding its own work and memory without changing the backend response.

gateway_port.description: Local gateway port for synthetic requests (1–65535). Defaults to the effective FERRUM_PROXY_HTTP_PORT (or FERRUM_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT when gateway_tls is enabled) resolved with the same environment > ferrum.conf/--settings precedence the listener itself uses, then 8000/8443. A resolved port of 0 (disabled listener) is rejected whichever configuration source supplied it. Serving nodes screen the 127.0.0.1 dial target with the backend egress policy, so a policy that denies loopback rejects the plugin unless 127.0.0.1 is allow-listed; control-plane admission checks the range only.

gateway_tls.description: Use HTTPS for local loopback synthetic requests

gateway_tls_no_verify.description: Skip TLS cert verification for loopback connections. Defaults to true when gateway_tls is enabled (gateway cert typically won't match 127.0.0.1)

items.description: An http(s) URL with a non-empty authority and no URL userinfo, query, or fragment. This pattern models only the intrinsic URL grammar the constructor admits; the environment-dependent checks below (loopback-alias equality against the selected local target, normalized duplicate origins, and backend egress screening) need runtime context and stay runtime-only.

gateway_addresses.description: Remote gateway URLs for one-hop fan-out from the originating controller (at most 32). Peers receive X-Loadtesting-Fanout and never re-fanout. Entries must be unique http(s) URLs without userinfo, query, or fragment. Local-loopback aliases of the selected local target (127/8, IPv4-mapped loopback, ::1, localhost, and names beneath .localhost with matching scheme and effective port) are rejected. Fan-out sends the trigger key and the triggering request's headers (credentials included) and body, so an http:// entry is admitted only to a loopback IP literal written as a dotted-quad 127.d.d.d or [::1] unless allow_plaintext is true. Each fan-out call is a single attempt bounded by duration_seconds and cancelled with the local run.

allow_plaintext.description: Admit an http:// gateway_addresses entry whose host is not a loopback IP literal. The trigger key and the triggering request's credentials then cross the network in clear.
